module_docs: SIMD Unicode validation and transcoding, plus base64, in Zig with no C.

symbols.name: Error
symbols.docs:
Why an input was rejected. The UTF kinds and their positions match
simdutf's `error_code` and `result`, so simdutf is a differential oracle.

symbols.name: header_bits
symbols.docs: A UTF-8 byte of the form 11111xxx.

symbols.name: too_short
symbols.docs: A UTF-8 sequence that ends before its continuation bytes do.

symbols.name: too_long
symbols.docs: A continuation byte where none was expected.

symbols.name: overlong
symbols.docs:
A UTF-8 sequence longer than the shortest one for its code point,
including the leads 0xC0 and 0xC1.

symbols.name: too_large
symbols.docs:
A code point above U+10FFFF, including 4-byte sequences led by
0xF5-0xF7.

symbols.name: surrogate
symbols.docs:
A surrogate code point (U+D800-U+DFFF) in UTF-8 or UTF-32, or an
unpaired surrogate in UTF-16.

symbols.name: not_ascii
symbols.docs: A byte above 0x7F where only ASCII is allowed.

symbols.name: invalid_base64_character
symbols.docs: A byte that is not in the base64 alphabet and not ignorable space.

symbols.name: base64_input_remainder
symbols.docs: Base64 input whose last chunk cannot be decoded under the options.

symbols.name: base64_extra_bits
symbols.docs: Base64 input with nonzero bits in the padding position.

symbols.name: output_buffer_too_small
symbols.docs: The output buffer is smaller than the operation needs.

symbols.name: fail
symbols.signature: pub fn fail(err: Error, position: usize) Result

symbols.name: ConvertResult
symbols.docs:
What a checked conversion reports: `err` and `count` as in `Result`,
simdutf's `result`, and the output code units written, which on failure
are the conversion of the input before `count`, as simdutf's
`full_result` has them in `output_count`. A caller that resumes after an
error, or stops at one, reads both: `count` input units are done and
`written` output units hold them.

symbols.name: count
symbols.docs:
The output code units written on success, the error's index in input
code units on failure.

symbols.name: written
symbols.docs:
The output code units written: `count` on success, the conversion of
the input before the error on failure.

symbols.name: fail
symbols.signature: pub fn fail(err: Error, position: usize, written: usize) ConvertResult

symbols.name: result
symbols.docs: The `Result` simdutf's `_with_errors` conversion returns.

symbols.name: scalar
symbols.docs:
Scalar reference implementations, one code unit at a time. They define
the expected result for every SIMD path: a SIMD function must return
exactly what its scalar counterpart returns, error kind and position
included, on every input.

symbols.name: validateUtf8
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-8, classifying errors exactly as simdutf's scalar
`validate_with_errors` does, so simdutf can serve as a differential
oracle. On failure `count` is the index of the first byte of the
ill-formed sequence.

symbols.name: validateAscii
symbols.docs:
Validates ASCII. On failure `count` is the index of the first byte above
0x7F.

symbols.name: validateUtf16le
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-16 stored little-endian. On failure `count` is the index of
the unpaired surrogate: a low one with no high one before it, or a high
one not followed by a low one.

symbols.name: validateUtf16be
symbols.docs: Validates UTF-16 stored big-endian, as `validateUtf16le` does.

symbols.name: validateUtf32
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-32 in native byte order. On failure `count` is the index of
the first value above U+10FFFF or in the surrogate range.

symbols.name: scalar_convert
symbols.docs:
Scalar reference transcoders and length functions, one code point at a
time. They define the result of every conversion: each SIMD path in
`convert.zig` and `length.zig` returns exactly what its counterpart here
returns, error kind and position included, on every input.

A checked conversion (`utf8ToUtf16`, ...) validates as it converts and
stops at the first ill-formed character, with simdutf's error kind and the
index of that character in the input. Before writing a character it checks
that the output has room for it, and fails with `output_buffer_too_small`
at that character's index when it does not. On either failure the output
holds the conversion of everything before it, and the `ConvertResult`
says how many code units that is. A buffer sized by the matching length
function never fails that way, even on invalid input, because the length
functions count every prefix at least as large as it converts.

A valid conversion (`validUtf8ToUtf16`, ...) assumes well-formed input and
an output buffer the matching length function sized; it returns the number
of code units written.

UTF-16 functions take the byte order of the code units in memory as a
comptime `Endian`, as simdutf's `char16_t` functions do. UTF-32 is native.

symbols.signature: pub inline fn swap16(comptime e: Endian, unit: u16) u16
symbols.docs:
A UTF-16 code unit stored in byte order `e`, as a native value, or a
native value as one stored in byte order `e`: the same swap both ways.

symbols.name: convert
symbols.docs:
Transcoding between UTF-8, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32, and Latin-1, with
SIMD. Callers own every buffer; nothing allocates.

Each conversion has two forms. The checked form (`utf8ToUtf16le`)
validates as it converts and returns a `ConvertResult`: on success the
number of code units written, on failure simdutf's error kind and the
index in the input of the first ill-formed character, and either way the
code units written, which on failure hold the input before the error.
When the output runs out it fails with `output_buffer_too_small` at the
first character that does not fit; a buffer sized by the matching
`length` function always fits. The valid form (`validUtf8ToUtf16le`)
assumes well-formed input and a buffer the `length` function sized, and
returns the number of code units written.
Results equal those of `scalar_convert.zig` on every input.

UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE name the byte order of the code units in memory, as
simdutf's `char16_t` functions do; UTF-32 is native.

The kernels follow Lemire and Muła, "Transcoding Billions of Unicode
Characters per Second with SIMD Instructions" (2022), and on AVX-512 with
VBMI2 Clausecker and Lemire, "Transcoding Unicode Characters with AVX-512
Instructions" (2023). UTF-8 is decoded a 64-byte block at a time: each
byte gets the value of a character ending there, and the values that end
characters are packed by shuffle tables keyed by the end-of-character mask
(by lane compression on AVX-512), with 12-byte windows for the tail.
UTF-16 and UTF-32 are encoded by expanding code points into lanes and
packing them, with ASCII and two-byte fast paths. UTF-8 is validated in
the same pass with Keiser and Lemire's three-lookup check. Every table is
built at comptime.

returns exactly what its counterpart in `scalar_convert.zig` returns; on

symbols.name: base64
symbols.docs:
Base64 encoding and decoding with SIMD, after Muła and Lemire, "Faster
Base64 Encoding and Decoding Using AVX2 Instructions" (2018), and "Base64
encoding and decoding at almost the speed of a memory copy" (2020) for
AVX-512 VBMI. Each step of the main loops turns 48 bytes into 64
characters or back; the last step works on a zero-padded block and writes
only what the input fills, so short inputs take the same vector code.
Decoding skips ASCII whitespace as WHATWG's forgiving-base64 does: a
block with whitespace has it compressed out into a staging buffer, which
is decoded once it holds 64 characters. The scalar reference in
`scalar_base64.zig` takes over at errors and at an output buffer too
small to finish in vectors, and every path here returns exactly what it
returns.

symbols.name: scalar
symbols.docs:
Scalar base64, one character at a time: the reference every SIMD path in
`base64.zig` must match, result and error position included. Decoding
follows WHATWG forgiving-base64 and the TC39 `Uint8Array.fromBase64`
last-chunk rules, with simdutf's `base64_to_binary` error kinds and
positions.

symbols.name: space
symbols.docs: A character's 6-bit value, or `space` or `invalid`.

symbols.name: decodeTable
symbols.docs:
The decoding table: each byte's value, `space` for the ASCII whitespace
WHATWG's forgiving-base64 skips (tab, LF, FF, CR, space), and `invalid`
for everything else, `=` included.

symbols.name: Trim
symbols.docs:
Where the encoded data ends: the input with trailing whitespace and up to
two trailing `=` (with whitespace between them) cut off, as simdutf cuts
them. A `=` left inside `src[0..len]` is an invalid character. `pad` is
the index of the first `=` cut off, or `len` without padding.

symbols.name: decode
symbols.signature: pub fn decode(dst: []u8, src: []const u8, options: DecodeOptions) Result
symbols.docs:
Decodes base64 `src` into `dst`, skipping ASCII whitespace.

On success `count` is the number of bytes written. On failure it is a
position in `src`: for `invalid_base64_character`, the offending
character, which includes a misplaced `=` and the first of trailing
padding that does not fit the last chunk; for `base64_input_remainder`
and `base64_extra_bits`, the end of the encoded data, before any trailing
padding and whitespace; for `output_buffer_too_small`, the first character
of the chunk that does not fit, where decoding can resume. `dst` needs at
most `maxDecodedLen(src.len)` bytes. On failure the contents of `dst` are
unspecified.

symbols.name: decodeFrom
symbols.signature: pub fn decodeFrom(dst: []u8, src: []const u8, t: Trim, start: usize, out: usize, options: DecodeOptions) Result
symbols.docs:
Decodes `src[i..t.len]` into `dst[o..]` and finishes the input, where
`t` is `trim(src)` and `i` starts a chunk: the characters before it, less
whitespace, are a multiple of four and already decoded into `dst[0..o]`.
SIMD paths call it for the part of the input they leave.

symbols.docs: The number of characters `encode` writes for `n` bytes.

symbols.name: maxDecodedLen
symbols.docs:
The most bytes `decode` can write for `n` input characters, whatever

symbols.name: encode
symbols.signature: pub fn encode(dst: []u8, src: []const u8, options: EncodeOptions) usize
symbols.docs:
Encodes `src` into `dst` and returns the number of characters written,
`encodedLen(src.len, options)`. `dst` must hold that many.

symbols.name: decode
symbols.signature: pub fn decode(dst: []u8, src: []const u8, options: DecodeOptions) Result
symbols.docs:
Decodes base64 `src` into `dst`, skipping ASCII whitespace (tab, LF, FF,
CR, and space), with padding optional unless `options.last_chunk` is
`.strict`.

On success `count` is the number of bytes written. On failure it is a
position in `src`: for `invalid_base64_character`, the offending
character, which includes a misplaced `=`; for `base64_input_remainder`
and `base64_extra_bits`, the end of the encoded data; for
`output_buffer_too_small`, the first character of the chunk that does not
fit, where decoding can resume with more room. A `dst` of
`maxDecodedLen(src.len)` bytes always fits. On failure the contents of
`dst` are unspecified.

`dst` may start where `src` does, to decode in place, with the same
result as decoding into a buffer of its own; on failure the contents of
`src` are then unspecified too. Otherwise the two must not overlap.

symbols.name: Isa
symbols.docs:
The instruction sets with a kernel here. `generic` is plain `@Vector`
code for any target; the others call LLVM intrinsics for byte lookups,
permutes, and multiply-adds, so they need the LLVM backend.

symbols.name: validate
symbols.docs:
Validation of UTF-8, ASCII, UTF-16LE/BE, and UTF-32, with SIMD.

Each function checks 64-byte blocks and stops at the first block that
fails. Inputs of four blocks or more check their first block unaligned
and the rest from the next 64-byte boundary, so no load splits a cache
line; a final partial block is the last 64 bytes of the input,
overlapping the block before it. Inputs shorter than a block are
zero-padded into one. The `WithErrors` forms find the position in the
failing block: ASCII, UTF-16, and UTF-32 from its lane masks, UTF-8 by
rerunning the scalar validator in `scalar.zig` from the last character
boundary before it, so error kinds and positions are exactly the scalar
validators'.

symbols.name: utf8
symbols.docs: Reports whether `bytes` is well-formed UTF-8.

symbols.name: utf8WithErrors
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-8. On failure `count` is the index of the first byte of the
ill-formed sequence, and `err` says what is wrong with it.

symbols.name: ascii
symbols.docs: Reports whether every byte is below 0x80.

symbols.name: asciiWithErrors
symbols.docs:
Validates ASCII. On failure `count` is the index of the first byte above
0x7F.

symbols.name: utf16le
symbols.docs: Reports whether `units` is well-formed UTF-16 stored little-endian.

symbols.name: utf16leWithErrors
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-16 stored little-endian. On failure `count` is the index of
the unpaired surrogate.

symbols.name: utf16be
symbols.docs: Reports whether `units` is well-formed UTF-16 stored big-endian.

symbols.name: utf16beWithErrors
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-16 stored big-endian. On failure `count` is the index of
the unpaired surrogate.

symbols.name: utf32
symbols.docs:
Reports whether every value is a Unicode scalar value: at most U+10FFFF
and not a surrogate.

symbols.name: utf32WithErrors
symbols.docs:
Validates UTF-32 in native byte order. On failure `count` is the index of
the first value above U+10FFFF (`too_large`) or in the surrogate range
(`surrogate`).
